newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-president says Iran has sent squad to kill him.
newsitem.headline: Ex-president says Iran has sent squad to kill him.

text.p: Exiled former Iranian President Abolhassan Bani-Sadr said on Sunday Tehran had sent a squad to kill him and some of its members were believed to be in Germany.
"We have received information that Tehran has ordered a commando to "execute' Bani-Sadr," the former president told Reuters in a telephone interview from his home near Paris.
A spokesman for the Iranian embassy in Paris denied the charge. "This is an absolute lie," he said.
Bani-Sadr said orders to assassinate him were given after he testified at the Berlin trial of five men accused of murdering three Iranian Kurdish dissidents and their translator in 1992.
He said he had known about the plot for a month and had passed on the names and descriptions of the six would-be assassins to French police.
"The latest information we had two days ago was that four of these men were believed to be in Germany," he said.
Asked who gave the alleged orders to kill him, he said: "Who else than (Supreme Iranian leader Ayatollah Ali) Khameini?"
Bani-Sadr said he did not know whether French police had reinforced his security. "I don't know. I never ask," he said.
He said at the Berlin trial that the killings of the Kurdish dissidents had been ordered by Khamenei and Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and prepared by Iranian secret services.

Several exiled opponents of the Iranian government have been murdered in France, among them the ousted shah's last prime minister Shapour Bakhtiar, knifed to death at his home near Paris in 1991. Tehran denies responsibility for the killings.
Bani-Sadr, elected Iran's first president after the 1979 Islamic revolution which pushed the shah from power, went into exile in France in 1981.
